# Terraform Enterprise cloud provider considerations

Use this page to find documented cloud deployment paths and provider constraints before you choose a Terraform Enterprise runtime.

## Support model

Select a supported Terraform Enterprise runtime and version from the [deployment overview](/terraform/enterprise/deploy) and [system requirements](https://www.ibm.com/software/reports/compatibility/clarity/index.html?name=IBM%20Terraform%20Self-Managed), then use the sections below for provider-specific guidance.

## Instructions per cloud provider

Refer to the following topics for instructions on configuring your Terraform Enterprise deployment for supported cloud providers.

### Amazon Web Services

- [Deploy Terraform Enterprise to Kubernetes](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/kubernetes) includes an Amazon EKS example.
- [Configure network access](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/network#disable-access-to-ec2-instance-metadata-service) describes how to prevent Docker containers from accessing the EC2 instance metadata service.
- [External log forwarding](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/manage/monitor/logs#external-log-forwarding) describes the AWS-only requirements for native CloudWatch and S3 destinations.

### Microsoft Azure

- [Deploy Terraform Enterprise to Kubernetes](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/kubernetes) includes an Azure Kubernetes Service (AKS) example and AKS Workload Identity guidance.
- [Deploy Terraform Enterprise to OpenShift](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/openshift) includes an Azure-based OpenShift example.
- [Azure Managed Identity requirements](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/storage/connect-database/postgres#azure-managed-identity-requirements) describes PostgreSQL authentication limitations.
- [Azure Redis requirements](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/storage/connect-redis#azure-requirements) describes the separate main and Sidekiq instance requirement.

### Google Cloud Platform

- [Deploy Terraform Enterprise to Kubernetes](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/kubernetes) includes a Google Kubernetes Engine (GKE) example.
- [Increase Terraform Enterprise run capacity on Kubernetes](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/kubernetes/scale/run-capacity#google-cloud-platform-kubernetes-engine-with-autopilot) includes GKE Autopilot guidance.
- [Configure network access](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/network#specify-additional-configuration-settings) describes the Docker MTU requirement.
- [Google Default Credentials](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/storage/connect-database/postgres#google-default-credentials) describes the Cloud SQL IAM requirements.
- [External log forwarding](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/manage/monitor/logs#external-log-forwarding) describes the GCP-only requirement for native Cloud Logging.

### IBM Cloud

Follow the standard [Kubernetes](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/kubernetes) workflow for IKS or [OpenShift](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/openshift) workflow for ROKS.

The following considerations apply only when you select the corresponding IBM Cloud service or deployment option:

- If you use IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL, follow the [IBM Cloud Databases for PostgreSQL](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/storage/connect-database/postgres#ibm-cloud-databases-for-postgresql) instructions.
- If you use IBM Cloud Databases for Redis, configure authentication and TLS for its private endpoint.
- If you use IBM Cloud Object Storage, configure the S3-compatible endpoint and HMAC credentials.
- If you mirror images to a private IBM Cloud Container Registry, select a plan with enough capacity and follow the [Kubernetes image configuration guidance](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/reference/configuration#kubernetes-specific-settings) for mirrored images and pull secrets.
- If you install through IBM Passport Advantage Online, follow the [IBM license and registry access instructions](/terraform/enterprise/deploy/configuration/license).
